accepted_edits.reason: Versions 2 to 4 apply the lead's read-only instruction and answer the four content-review findings; sections 3 and 4 are un-deferred with the repository search added to section 3.

findings.reason: a worker dispatched to §2 reads a parked plan with an implementable section and cannot tell whether to build, so the section either stalls on a settled prerequisite or ships against a gate the author still believes unmet.
findings.text: the lead and the eyebrow (line 32) say the plan is parked until credentials and the identity are settled, while the two decisions dated 2026-11-15T20:56:15 record credentials stored (line 67) and the lead's own account chosen for development (line 76), and §2 is declared `implementable` (line 45); the same snapshot therefore states two different gates

findings.reason: if the instance serves only an HTML page, §2 cannot produce its declared figures and cannot close; the deliverable must name the description as the instance actually serves it, or §2 must first establish that a machine-readable description exists.
findings.text: §1's only cited evidence is that two documentation *pages* sit behind the login gate, and it concludes "the API's own documentation page is therefore the specification", yet §2 (line 46) requires a machine-readable description and its done-when (line 47) counts "the number of operations in the description"; nothing in §1 establishes that the instance serves a machine-readable description, so §2's central figure and read-operation list may be unobtainable

findings.reason: the block binds only if the blocked plan records the dependency; as written §4 there is dispatchable and will fail on exactly the access route this plan exists to create, or this plan's claim of what blocks is wrong.
findings.text: this plan declares it blocks `iter-signal-context-and-enrichment`, but that plan's `plan-section-depends-on` never names `icp-api-access`, its §4 is `implementable` and asserts the content "reaches the graph from ICP and IDM through the project's existing authenticated document access" (line 59), directly contradicting this plan's "A build worker cannot reach either today" (line 34)

findings.reason: without the leak check a §3 run can commit ICP-derived records to the tracked tree and still close, so the plan's stated containment constraint has no measure in the section most likely to violate it.
findings.text: §1 (line 42) requires that none of the ICP content enter the repository and §4's done-when (line 57) includes "a search of the tracked tree finds none of the fetched content", but §3's done-when has no such search even though it returns typed plant-structure records a worker can cache as fixtures
